regions.summary: Lankao county on the old Yellow River plain (73%), plus the Shandong edge of Cao county (25%).

candidates.name: Lankao
candidates.meaning: Merger name (1954) of Lanfeng (from Lanyang and Yifeng) and Kaocheng counties; known for its paulownia trees and as Jiao Yulu's county.
candidates.fit: Region holds 98% of Lankao's people and Lankao is 73% of the region.
candidates.recognisability: Current county.
candidates.source_note: 今日兰考县就是由历史上的兰封县（由兰阳县、仪封县合并）、考城县合并而成

candidates.name: Cao
candidates.meaning: Cao county in Shandong, named after the Cao state and Caozhou prefecture (reduced to a county in 1371).
candidates.fit: Holds 25% of the region's people but only 17% of Cao county; most of Cao lies in a Shandong region.
candidates.recognisability: Current county.
candidates.source_note: 明洪武四年（1371年），降曹州为曹县

regions.notes: The Shandong part of the region is Cao county, so check the Heze neighbour in the Shandong batch does not also take 'Cao'.

regions.summary: North-west Zhengzhou on the Yellow River bank: Huiji district, Guxing, the Mang hills.

candidates.name: Huiji
candidates.meaning: "Benefit and relief": named in 2004 after Huiji Bridge, a three-arch stone bridge on the Guangji canal (the district was Mangshan district before).
candidates.fit: Huiji is 59% of the region's people, and the region holds 64% of the district.
candidates.recognisability: Current district.
candidates.source_note: 区名来源于位于区内的惠济桥

candidates.name: Mangshan
candidates.meaning: The Mang loess ridge along the south bank of the Yellow River; the district was called Mangshan district until 2004.
candidates.fit: The ridge lies in the north-west of the region (Guxing, the Yellow River scenic area), but the name is far more associated with Luoyang.
candidates.recognisability: Own zh-wiki article; 465 hits with Zhengzhou, top ones about the Luoyang tombs.
candidates.source_note: 惠济区，原名邙山区；邙山丘陵位于区西北部

regions.notes: Mangshan is likely to be wanted by the Luoyang (west) batch.

regions.summary: North-east Zhengzhou: Jinshui district's Zhengdong new area, Longzi lake, Huayuankou on the Yellow River.

candidates.name: Jinshui
candidates.meaning: "Gold water": the Jinshui River, a canal dug in the early Song to bring water to Kaifeng (west is the metal direction).
candidates.fit: Jinshui is 92% of the region's people and the region holds 53% of the district.
candidates.recognisability: Current district; the Henan provincial government sits in it.
candidates.source_note: 金水区的名称来源于金水河

candidates.name: Huayuankou
candidates.meaning: A Yellow River village where the dike was deliberately breached in 1938, flooding three provinces.
candidates.fit: The town holds only 3% of the region, on its northern edge.
candidates.recognisability: Own zh-wiki article; 179 hits with Zhengzhou, mostly the 1938 breach and a Zhengzhou road.
candidates.source_note: 花园口镇位于郑州市区东北角的黄河南岸

candidates.name: Zhengdong
candidates.meaning: "East of Zhengzhou": the Zhengdong New Area planned in 2002 over the east of Jinshui.
candidates.fit: Most of the region is the new area, but the name reads as part of a whole.
candidates.recognisability: New-area name, not an admin unit.
candidates.source_note: 2002年，郑东新区的规划启动，辖区东部……目前由郑东新区代管

regions.summary: Kaifeng city proper: Gulou, Longting, Shunhe, Yuwangtai, Jinming.

candidates.name: Kaifeng
candidates.meaning: "Open the frontier": from Qifeng, a town Duke Zhuang of Zheng built to push his borders; renamed under the Han to avoid Emperor Jing's name Qi.
candidates.fit: Holds the old walled city and 25% of the prefecture's people; the prefecture's urban centre.
candidates.recognisability: Prefecture city; capital of the Northern Song.
candidates.source_note: 取“启拓封疆”之义……以开代启而改名为开封

candidates.name: Bianliang
candidates.meaning: Liang on the Bian River: the Song capital (Dongjing) as later called under the Yuan, when it was Bianliang circuit.
candidates.fit: Seat of Bianliang circuit (1288-1367) was exactly this city.
candidates.recognisability: Own zh-wiki article, 208 hits with Kaifeng, all about this place.
candidates.source_note: 汴梁指北宋首都东京開封府治所，即「汴京」，现河南省开封市

regions.summary: Zhongmu county (74%) between Zhengzhou and Kaifeng, plus a slice of Guancheng.

candidates.name: Zhongmu
candidates.meaning: Old place name (Mou in the middle); a county since the early Western Han, formerly called Putian and Mouzhou.
candidates.fit: Zhongmu is 74% of the region; the region holds 59% of the county and its county seat.
candidates.recognisability: Current county; site of the Battle of Guandu.
candidates.source_note: 中牟县，古称“圃田”、“牟州”

regions.summary: West of Zhengzhou on the Yellow River: Xingyang (58%), Gongyi (26%), Shangjie, Hulao pass.

candidates.name: Xingyang
candidates.meaning: Yang (north bank) of the Xing marsh, from the Yu Gong line "the Xing banks are pooled"; Han Xingyang commandery.
candidates.fit: Xingyang is 58% of the region and the region holds 88% of its people; Xingyang commanderies (493-582) were seated in the old town here.
candidates.recognisability: Current county-level city; origin of the Xingyang Zheng clan.
candidates.source_note: 荥阳之名取自《尚书·禹贡》中的“荥陂既潴”

candidates.name: Hulao
candidates.meaning: "Tiger pen": the pass on the Yellow River south bank guarding the road to Luoyang (also Si River pass, Chenggao pass).
candidates.fit: Pass lies at Sishui in the far west of Xingyang, inside the region, but is a small part of its people.
candidates.recognisability: Own zh-wiki article; 29 hits with Xingyang, top ones about this place.
candidates.source_note: 今河南省荥阳市市区西北部16公里的汜水镇境内

candidates.name: Gongyi
candidates.meaning: Gong county on the Luo River mouth, "lock and key of the eastern capital".
candidates.fit: 26% of the region but only 30% of Gongyi's people; the rest lies in the region to the west.
candidates.recognisability: Current county-level city.
candidates.source_note: 巩义因地扼古都洛阳，故历史上有“东都锁钥”之称

regions.notes: The west batch will probably name a Gongyi region; this one keeps Xingyang.

regions.summary: The old centre of Zhengzhou: Jinshui south, Erqi Square, Zhengzhou railway station area.

candidates.name: Zhengzhou
candidates.meaning: From the Zheng state; the name moved from Xinzheng to this city in the Sui and Tang, replacing the older name Guancheng.
candidates.fit: Most central region, holding the prefecture seat since 607 and the main station; 5.6M city.
candidates.recognisability: Provincial capital.
candidates.source_note: 郑州古称管城，隋开皇三年……将荥州更名为郑州

regions.summary: West-central Zhengzhou: Zhongyuan district's government centre, cotton mills, universities, part of Erqi.

candidates.name: Zhongyuan
candidates.meaning: "Central plain": the district was named in 1961 after the commune; the term is the traditional name for the Yellow River heartland.
candidates.fit: Zhongyuan is 60% of the region and the district government sits here; the region holds 40% of the district.
candidates.recognisability: Current district; the word is the common name for the whole plain.
candidates.source_note: 中原区始建于1948年……区人民政府驻桐柏路200号

regions.notes: Zhongyuan also covers 66% of region 10; I gave 10 a river name instead. The other Henan batches may reach for 'Zhongyuan' as a plain name; it is better kept here.

regions.summary: Guancheng old town and the Shang city area, Zhengzhou's south-east.

candidates.name: Guancheng
candidates.meaning: "Guan city": after the Guan state of Guan Shu, King Wu's brother; Guancheng county and Guanzhou from 596.
candidates.fit: Guancheng Hui district is 74% of the region, the region holds 62% of the district, and the old walled town (Guancheng street) is here.
candidates.recognisability: Current district; Zhengzhou's old name.
candidates.source_note: 周武王封其弟姬鲜于此为王，称为管国……隋开皇十六年设立管城县

regions.notes: CHGIS puts the Guancheng seat in region 8 only because of coordinate rounding; the old town is Guancheng district.

regions.summary: West Zhengzhou: Shifo, Xiliu Lake, Mazhai, Zhengzhou's high-tech zone, a bit of Xingyang.

candidates.name: Jialu
candidates.meaning: Named after Jia Lu, the Yuan works minister who dredged it; rises in Xinmi, flows north-east through west Zhengzhou, then east.
candidates.fit: The river runs down the west side of Zhengzhou through this region (also touching 2, 5 and 13).
candidates.recognisability: Own zh-wiki article; 72 hits with Zhengzhou, top ones about this river's stations and metro lines.
candidates.source_note: 发源于新密市境内，向东北流经郑州市区西部后折向东流

candidates.name: Xushui
candidates.meaning: The Xu River, joining the Suo to form the Suoxu River; Xushui county (621-626) was seated west of Zhengzhou.
candidates.fit: Xushui street and the Xu River are in the middle of the region, but the name is minor.
candidates.recognisability: No own article; 71 hits with Zhengzhou, mostly metro stations and a street.
candidates.source_note: 须水县 (621-626) 今郑州市西须水镇 (CHGIS); 索须河因索河和须水两河汇流而得名

regions.notes: Weakest region of the batch for names; Zhongyuan (66% of it) is used for region 8. Jialu might also be wanted by the Zhoukou region it ends in.

regions.summary: South Zhengzhou: Erqi district south of the station, Guancheng south, Xinzheng's Longhu.

candidates.name: Erqi
candidates.meaning: "February 7": the 1923 Beijing-Hankou railway strike; the district was named for it in 1955.
candidates.fit: Erqi is 56% of the region and the region holds 47% of the district; the memorial tower itself is in region 7.
candidates.recognisability: Current district; the strike is a standard history topic.
candidates.source_note: 1955年10月为纪念二七大罢工而改称二七区

regions.notes: No second name I could source for this one.

regions.summary: Rural Kaifeng: Xiangfu district (old Kaifeng county, 49%) and Tongxu county (46%).

candidates.name: Tongxu
candidates.meaning: "Leading to the Xu land": a Song canal town, named when the Cai River was dredged from the capital towards the old Xu country (1189 name).
candidates.fit: Tongxu is 46% of the region and the region holds 96% of the county.
candidates.recognisability: Current county.
candidates.source_note: 取自汴京直通许国故地之义，故名通许

candidates.name: Chenliu
candidates.meaning: Chenliu commandery and county (Han to Qing): the county town and its Prince of Chenliu title; the Chenliu town lies in the region.
candidates.fit: Chenliu county (221 BC-1911) was seated at Chenliu town in Xiangfu, and the commandery covered Xiangfu, Tongxu and Lankao.
candidates.recognisability: En-wiki 'Chenliu' town plus 'Prince of Chenliu'; 210 zh hits with Kaifeng, about this area.
candidates.source_note: 陈留县 (221 BC-1911) 今河南开封县东南陈留镇; 陈留郡 (122 BC-187)

candidates.name: Xiangfu
candidates.meaning: "Auspicious omen": the Song Dazhongxiangfu reign name, given to Kaifeng's county in 1009; today's Xiangfu district.
candidates.fit: Xiangfu holds 49% of the region, but the name belongs to Kaifeng city's own history.
candidates.recognisability: Current district; also an old name for Kaifeng itself.
candidates.source_note: 以年号改浚仪县为祥符县

regions.summary: Weishi county (58%) and the Zhongmu side south-east of Zhengzhou, with Guandu.

candidates.name: Weishi
candidates.meaning: From the town of the Zheng official Weishi (the military commandant); a county since the Qin.
candidates.fit: Weishi is 58% of the region and the region holds 66% of the county.
candidates.recognisability: Current county.
candidates.source_note: 县境在春秋时期为郑国大夫尉氏之邑，因而得名

candidates.name: Guandu
candidates.meaning: "Official ford": a town in Zhongmu where Cao Cao beat Yuan Shao in 200.
candidates.fit: Guandu town is in this region but is under 7% of its people.
candidates.recognisability: Own zh-wiki article; 376 hits with Zhongmu, top ones about the battle and the town.
candidates.source_note: 官渡是从河北进军河南地界的军事要冲之地，因为发生了官渡大战而闻名

candidates.name: Zhongmu
candidates.meaning: See region 5.
candidates.fit: 28% of the region but only 35% of Zhongmu; the county seat and the rest are region 5.
candidates.recognisability: Current county.
candidates.source_note: 中牟县，古称“圃田”、“牟州”

regions.summary: Qi county (77%) in the east, with a part of Sui county (19%).

candidates.name: Qixian
candidates.meaning: County named for the Qi state (the Xia descendants' fief), formerly Yongqiu; the Chinese phrase 'worrying that the sky falls' comes from it.
candidates.fit: Qi is 77% of the region and the region holds 85% of the county.
candidates.recognisability: Current county.
candidates.source_note: 杞县，古称雍丘……商周时为杞国

candidates.name: Yongqiu
candidates.meaning: The old county name for Qi county (Qin to Song), seat of Yangxia commandery and Qi prefecture, site of the 756 siege.
candidates.fit: Seat was Qi county town; the commandery and prefecture covered the county.
candidates.recognisability: No own article; 40 zh hits with Qi county, all about this place.
candidates.source_note: 秦统一六国后置雍丘县……北魏孝昌四年（528年）置阳夏郡，以雍丘县为郡治

regions.summary: Xinzheng city (88%) south-east of Zhengzhou, airport zone.

candidates.name: Xinzheng
candidates.meaning: "New Zheng": the capital the Zheng state moved to when it migrated east; later capital of Han; birthplace of the Yellow Emperor tradition.
candidates.fit: Xinzheng is 88% of the region and the region holds 51% of the city; the Zheng-Han city is just west.
candidates.recognisability: Current county-level city; the airport carries the name.
candidates.source_note: “新郑”之名源于周代诸侯国郑国东迁之事

regions.summary: Xinmi city (73%) in the Song foothills, with Xinzheng's western townships.

candidates.name: Xinmi
candidates.meaning: "New Mi": from the Mi state, named after Mi mountain; the county was Mixian until 1994.
candidates.fit: Xinmi is 73% of the region and the region holds 97% of the city.
candidates.recognisability: Current county-level city.
candidates.source_note: 新密西周时属密国，因“密山”得名

regions.summary: Dengfeng (73%) around Mount Song and Shaolin, plus north-west Yuzhou (27%).

candidates.name: Dengfeng
candidates.meaning: "Ascend and enfeoff": named by Empress Wu Zetian for her 696 sacrifice at Mount Song.
candidates.fit: Dengfeng is 73% of the region and the region holds 99% of the city.
candidates.recognisability: Current county-level city; Shaolin Temple.
candidates.source_note: 登封之名由武周女皇帝武则天所封

candidates.name: Songshan
candidates.meaning: "Lofty mountain": the central peak of the Five Sacred Mountains, split into Taishi and Shaoshi.
candidates.fit: The range lies wholly in Dengfeng, in the north of the region.
candidates.recognisability: Own zh-wiki article; 590 hits with Dengfeng, top ones about this place.
candidates.source_note: 中岳嵩山是境内北部的主要山脉，分为太室、少室二山

regions.notes: The west batch (Luoyang, Song county) might also want Songshan.

regions.summary: Changge city (64%) with Weishi's western townships and Xuchang county's north (Jian'an district).

candidates.name: Changge
candidates.meaning: "Long Ge": the old land of the legendary Getian clan; Zhuang of Zheng 'dug the ground to meet his mother' here; ancient Changshe.
candidates.fit: Changge (written Zhangge in facts.json) is 64% of the region and the region holds 94% of the city.
candidates.recognisability: Current county-level city.
candidates.source_note: 相传这里是上古时葛天氏的故地，后人便命名为长葛

regions.notes: facts.json spells it 'Zhangge'; the correct pinyin is Changge.

regions.summary: Yuzhou city (79%) on the Ying River, with Xiangcheng's north.

candidates.name: Yuzhou
candidates.meaning: "Yu's prefecture": after Yu the Great, whose Xia capital tradition is here; the Ming renamed Junzhou to avoid Emperor Wanli's name.
candidates.fit: Yuzhou is 79% of the region and the region holds 68% of the city.
candidates.recognisability: Current county-level city; homophone of Yuzhou (Henan's old name) written differently.
candidates.source_note: 夏启在此建立了中国历史上第一个世袭王朝夏朝……称颍州、钧州（避明神宗讳，改称禹州）

candidates.name: Yingchuan
candidates.meaning: "Ying river": the Qin-Han commandery named for the Ying River, seated at Yangzhai (Yuzhou); the heartland of this part of Henan.
candidates.fit: Seat at Yuzhou for 230 BC-220 AD; the commandery also covered Xuchang, Changge and Xiangcheng nearby.
candidates.recognisability: Own zh-wiki article; 174 hits with Xuchang, top ones about this commandery.
candidates.source_note: 因颍水流过境内而得名，治所在阳翟（今河南省禹州市）

candidates.name: Junzhou
candidates.meaning: Jin and Yuan prefecture (1184-1233 and after), source of Jun porcelain, one of the five famous Chinese wares.
candidates.fit: Prefecture seat was Yuzhou; Jun kilns are at Shenhou in the city.
candidates.recognisability: Named in zh-wiki as Yuzhou's old name (钧都); not distinct from Junzhou in Hubei.
candidates.source_note: 钧州 (州, 1184-1233) 今河南省禹州市; 钧瓷的唯一产地

regions.notes: Yingchuan could also fit Xuchang (20), so it should not be used twice.

regions.summary: Xuchang city: Weidou district (52%) and Jian'an district (47%).

candidates.name: Xuchang
candidates.meaning: Name from the ancient Xu state; renamed in the Wei ("Han fell by Xu, Wei flourished by Xu") from Xu county; the Han capital under Cao Cao.
candidates.fit: Holds the prefecture seat (Xuzhou since 581) and Weidou district entirely.
candidates.recognisability: Prefecture city.
candidates.source_note: 曹丕……将许县改称许昌县

candidates.name: Jian'an
candidates.meaning: Reign name of Emperor Xian of Han (196-220) when Xuchang was his capital; the district outside the city.
candidates.fit: Jian'an district is the rural 47% of the region; the name also marks the Jian'an poets.
candidates.recognisability: Current district.
candidates.source_note: 区名得名于东汉末代皇帝汉献帝刘协的年号——建安

regions.summary: Linying (44%) and Yanling (44%) in the plain east of Xuchang.

candidates.name: Linying
candidates.meaning: "Beside the Ying": the county lies on the Ying River; set up in 201 BC.
candidates.fit: Linying is 44% of the region and the region holds 67% of the county.
candidates.recognisability: Current county; Wei's Shoushan abdication altar is near.
candidates.source_note: 因濒临颍河得名

candidates.name: Yanling
candidates.meaning: From the Yan state (Zhou fief), renamed Yanling in the Eastern Zhou; known for Yanling plum and flower nurseries and the Jin-Chu Battle of Yanling.
candidates.fit: Yanling is 44% of the region and the region holds 89% of the county.
candidates.recognisability: Current county.
candidates.source_note: 周初封为鄢国，东周平王初改为鄢陵……晋楚鄢陵之战

regions.notes: The two counties are of equal size here; Anita picks.

regions.summary: Xiangcheng (41%), with Yancheng, Linying and Wuyang parts south-west of Luohe.

candidates.name: Xiangcheng
candidates.meaning: King Xiang of Zhou took refuge here and built a city; a county since the Qin.
candidates.fit: Xiangcheng is 41% of the region and the region holds 80% of the county; Xiangcheng commandery (266-582) was here.
candidates.recognisability: Current county.
candidates.source_note: 周襄王避王子带之乱，居于此，后筑城，秦代置襄城县

candidates.name: Yancheng
candidates.meaning: Yan city: site of Yue Fei's 1140 Yancheng victory; Luohe's seat district.
candidates.fit: 22% of the region but the seat and most of the district sit in region 23; spelling clashes with Yancheng (Jiangsu).
candidates.recognisability: Current district.
candidates.source_note: 岳飞“郾城大捷”的古战场

regions.notes: Xiangcheng also reads the same as Xiangcheng (项城) in Zhoukou in pinyin; check the east batch.

regions.summary: Luohe city: Yuanhui, Yancheng and Shaoling districts.

candidates.name: Luohe
candidates.meaning: The Luo River (Sha and Li rivers meet at the city); the prefecture-level city of 2.4M.
candidates.fit: Holds the urban core (Yuanhui 87% of the district) and the prefecture seat.
candidates.recognisability: Prefecture city.
candidates.source_note: 沙河、澧河、颍河、清潩河自西向东流经境内……沙河、澧河……在市区交汇

candidates.name: Shaoling
candidates.meaning: Site of the 656 BC Shaoling covenant between Duke Huan of Qi and Chu; home town of Xu Shen; the character 召 is read shao here.
candidates.fit: Han county seat at Shaoling; Shaoling district is 31% of the region (district written Zhaoling in facts.json).
candidates.recognisability: Own zh-wiki article; 394 hits with Luohe, top ones about this place.
candidates.source_note: 召陵区……是东汉许慎的故乡; 召陵之盟

regions.notes: Sha river itself is also an option if needed.
